stories.headline: Trumbull seeking poll workers for Nov. 3 in-person voting
stories.summary: Trumbull is recruiting poll workers ahead of the Nov. 3, 2026, general election to keep in-person voting safe and make sure every eligible ballot is counted. Duties include greeting and checking in voters, handing out ballots, guarding voting machines, and assisting voters with visual or mobility needs. Applicants must be at least 16, work the full day (5 a.m. to 9 p.m. or later), and attend a training session usually held the Wednesday evening before Election Day. Pay is $200–$350; the town provides lunch and dinner. Interested residents should call the elections office at 203-452-5058 or 5059.

stories.headline: Reuters: states wrongly added 30,000+ self-declared noncitizens to voter rolls
stories.summary: A Reuters review of official records finds U.S. states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to voter rolls since 2000 through software glitches and DMV clerical errors in both red and blue states. New Jersey alone cited a tech glitch that put about 6,600 noncitizens on rolls between 2023 and 2024; similar mistakes turned up in California, Texas, Iowa, Virginia, and others. Experts say the totals are tiny versus 170 million registered voters and rarely show ballots cast, but Heritage’s Don Palmer called agency errors the primary pathway for noncitizen registrations. The White House is pushing the SAVE America Act’s proof-of-citizenship rules ahead of the midterms.

stories.headline: Trump admin races to Supreme Court after third-country deportation flight canceled
stories.summary: After a late-night First Circuit clarification blocked third-country removals, the Trump administration filed an emergency Supreme Court appeal Thursday, saying a flight with about 70 deportees bound for three African countries had to be scrubbed. AG Todd Blanche called the order a dark-of-night strike on a legal tool; Solicitor General D. John Sauer warned of cascading delays and reworked foreign agreements. Lower courts require a meaningful chance for migrants to argue persecution or torture risk before third-country deportation. The justices previously let flights continue temporarily; the administration says thousands more remain eligible for removal.

stories.headline: Mother of ICE-shot Austin delivery driver describes video call after the shooting
stories.summary: Flor Pérez told Reuters her last contact with son Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was a Sunday video call moments after an ICE agent shot him during a vehicle stop in Austin. She heard him say agents crashed into his car and shot him, then watched an officer pull him out by the arm. Four days later he remains in ICE detention with the bullet still in his back; DHS says he is getting round-the-clock care while attorneys seek release before a Wednesday hearing. Rep. Greg Casar said the wound is packed with gauze changed multiple times a day. Federal agents have shot at least 20 people since Trump returned to office, seven fatally.

stories.headline: CT police standards council urges tighter rules on Flock license-plate cameras
stories.summary: Connecticut’s Police Officer Standards and Training Council sent Gov. Ned Lamont a 59-page report recommending stricter rules for Flock and other surveillance tech, including cutting license-plate data retention from 21 days to seven, two-factor access, audits, and limits on camera densification. About three-quarters of CT departments use fixed plate readers (1,564 cameras); Flock holds ~39% of the market. Chair Keith Mello said the tech works but privacy safeguards have not kept pace. Privacy activist Eric Weiner backed the recommendations yet argued cloud storage risks remain beyond local control. Lawmakers say the report will shape January legislation after an Oct. 1 privacy law already takes effect.

stories.headline: Tesla opens Nevada Semi factory aiming for 50,000 trucks a year
stories.summary: Tesla formally opened its first high-volume Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada, on Thursday, livestreaming the ribbon-cutting while Elon Musk appeared by video from a Washington state dinner with Trump and Xi. Semi engineering director Dan Priestley said the plant targets 50,000 trucks a year (~1,000/week) and more than 3,000 jobs during the ramp. Musk called the Semi “almost like a sports car in truck form” and reiterated FSD for Semi by late 2026 or early 2027 to address driver shortages. Fleet deals include a 2,500-truck ZET SCALE order and 500 for Einride; long-range Semis have been priced around $290,000 per ICCT.

stories.headline: Musk: SpaceX can take AI ‘pole position’ in about six months if growth holds
stories.summary: Responding to a critic who said SpaceXAI had already lost the race, Elon Musk argued Thursday that SpaceX’s AI effort is only three years old versus six for Anthropic and ten for OpenAI, and that a strong “second derivative” of progress could put it in pole position in about six months. He separately said he is cautiously optimistic SpaceX will have a “Fable/GPT-6 level model” within two to three months, stressed that excess intelligence is useless for simple tasks, and called compute the hard bottleneck—one SpaceX claims unique skill at solving, including orbital data-center ambitions. SpaceXAI also rolled out voice for its Grok Bot workplace agent this month.

stories.headline: watchOS 27.2 code hints at iPhone-style screenshot preview, share, delete
stories.summary: Code explorer pdfu found a disabled feature flag in watchOS 27.2 that would let Apple Watch screenshots show a preview with share or delete options, mirroring iPhone behavior. Today, pressing the Digital Crown and side button dumps a capture straight into iPhone Photos with no confirmation—easy to do by accident, and screenshots are off by default. MacRumors notes the change could land in a later 27.2 beta once the flag is enabled, giving Watch owners more control than a simple on/off toggle.

stories.headline: Insta360 Luna Ultra hits 22.5× zoom via free firmware and $49.99 telephoto clip-on
stories.summary: Insta360 pushed Luna Ultra’s digital zoom from 12× to 15× with a free firmware update that also improves telephoto stability and low-light concert modes, plus 4K vertical shooting on the Ultra’s 1-inch wide sensor. A new Ultra Telephoto Adapter ($49.99) clips over the dual-camera block, blocks the wide lens, and stretches reach to about 22.5× (~450mm equivalent). Digital Camera World’s hands-on says the adapter experience is quirky but impressive for a pocket gimbal; stock was already thin on Insta360’s store at publish time.

stories.headline: Canon Dual Pixel 3D Converter: free Windows app builds 3D models from one photo
stories.summary: Canon’s Dual Pixel 3D Converter, due as a free Windows 11 download on Oct. 8, 2026, turns a single Dual Pixel RAW (or distance-tagged R8 Mark II JPEG) into OBJ/GLB meshes or a short MP4 using left/right photodiode depth cues. Launch support covers eight EOS R bodies and twelve RF lenses; shoot around f/5.6, ISO ≤1600, with textured tabletop subjects. Luminous Landscape calls it partly a gimmick and partly a creative unlock for product shooters—no second lens or LiDAR required, but backsides stay invisible and Mac users wait.

stories.headline: LEGO’s 2026 Halloween wave: Mayor Manor, La Catrina, and a $100 haunted-tree gift
stories.summary: LEGO’s 2026 Halloween lineup spans $14.99 mini builds through adult sets, highlighted by Midnight Valley’s debut Mayor Manor (1,420 pieces), Ideas La Catrina (1,212), Botanicals Dark Flower Arrangement (562), plus Gremlins BrickHeadz, Nightmare Before Christmas, and Wednesday’s Thing’s Apartment. Smaller kits include a Jack-O’-Lantern pickup, Altar of the Dead, and Halloween Skull Candle. Spend $100 or more and LEGO throws in the Creator Scary Haunted Tree gift-with-purchase (valued at $19.99) with poseable arms, a light-up mouth, crow, and pumpkin.

stories.headline: Metallica extends M72 into spring 2027 stadiums with Limp Bizkit and Avatar
stories.summary: Metallica locked in 12 North American M72 stadium dates from May 8, 2027, at Vancouver’s BC Place through June 19 at Salt Lake City’s Rice-Eccles Stadium, with Limp Bizkit and Avatar supporting every show. Stops include San Diego, El Paso, San Antonio, Fayetteville, Kansas City, Raleigh, Indianapolis, Buffalo, Madison, and Cleveland after the band’s Sphere “Life Burns Faster” residency. Fan-club and card presales ran this week; general onsale is Friday, Sept. 25, at 10 a.m. local. A cut of every ticket still funds All Within My Hands charities.
